title: The Peer Review Problem
text:
Academic articles are usually evaluated by peer reviewers before publication. This process is designed to detect weak methodology and unsupported claims. However, reviewers are often under time pressure, which can limit the depth of their scrutiny. As a result, some flawed studies still reach print.

Readers of academic articles should therefore not accept every conclusion at face value. A careful reader examines whether the sample is representative and whether the results could have been produced by chance. Such scepticism is not hostility toward research but a necessary part of understanding it.

questions.text: According to the passage, what is the purpose of peer review?
options: To detect weak methodology and unsupported claims
To translate articles into other languages
To reduce the length of published articles
To replace the work of the original authors

questions.text: What questions does the passage say a careful reader should ask?
options: Whether the sample is representative and whether results could be due to chance
Whether the author is famous and whether the journal is expensive
Whether the article has colourful illustrations
Whether the conclusion is short and easy to remember

questions.text: Why does the passage suggest that some flawed studies still get published?
options: Reviewers may lack the time to examine studies thoroughly
Authors are never allowed to revise their work
Readers refuse to read academic articles

questions.text: What attitude toward research does the passage encourage?
options: Critical engagement rather than blind acceptance
Complete rejection of all published findings
Indifference to how studies are conducted

vocabulary.definition: careful and critical examination of something
containing errors or weaknesses that reduce its value
typical of a larger group or population
a questioning attitude that does not accept claims without evidence

paragraph_translations: Akademik makaleler genellikle yayımlanmadan önce hakem denetiminden geçer. Bu süreç, zayıf yöntemleri ve desteklenmemiş iddiaları tespit etmek için tasarlanmıştır. Ancak hakemler çoğu zaman zaman baskısı altındadır, bu da incelemelerinin derinliğini sınırlayabilir. Sonuç olarak, kusurlu bazı çalışmalar yine de basılmaktadır.

Akademik makalelerin okuyucuları, her sonucu olduğu gibi kabul etmemelidir. Dikkatli bir okuyucu, örneklemin temsil edici olup olmadığını ve sonuçların tesadüfen ortaya çıkıp çıkamayacağını sorgular. Bu tür bir şüphecilik araştırmaya karşı düşmanlık değil, onu anlamanın gerekli bir parçasıdır.
